representation_comparisons.result_summary: The embedding-based Genolator (full) outperformed the GPT-4.1 classifier receiving DNA and amino-acid sequences as plain text, although the systems also differ in backbone, training, and included modalities.

evidence.quote: In previous work 30 , we demonstrated that sequence embeddings capture significant information but may not encompass all relevant biological features needed for various downstream tasks. To address this, we adopt an intermediate fusion strategy 31,32 , combining four distinct modalities: the  DNA sequence, the amino acid sequence, the 3D protein structure of the target gene or protein, and the user's natural language query.

representation_rationale.summary: The authors use intermediate fusion of DNA, amino-acid, structure, and natural-language modalities because sequence embeddings may omit relevant biological features.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, Evo2 22 , the model used to generate DNA embeddings for Genolator, offers a substantially larger input size (1 million) compared  to the nucleotide transformer model  (12 kb) 24 . This was  especially advantageous for Genolator, as it enabled the encoding of complete genes, including introns and UTR  regions

representation_rationale.summary: The authors favor Evo2 because its larger context window can encode complete genes, including introns and UTR regions.

evidence.quote: A key advantage of our approach is the demonstrated value of foundation models like Evo2 22 , which  can  generate  highly  informative  embeddings  for  downstream  tasks  without  requiring additional fine-tuning. This flexibility  allows  for  rapid  migration  or  replacement  of  embedding models, as well as straightforward retraining.

representation_rationale.summary: Frozen foundation-model embeddings are presented as informative, reusable, and efficient to migrate or replace.

evidence.quote: Firstly, the DNA embeddings (Evo2 22 ) had the highest information content, as they incorporated non-coding regions (such as introns and UTRs) and were produced by the most extensive of the three foundation models.

representation_rationale.summary: The authors attribute the stronger attention to Evo2 to its higher information content and inclusion of non-coding regions.

evidence.quote: Consequently, projecting the highly condensed structural embeddings (128 dimensions) into a much larger space (4096 dimensions) may not provide as much meaningful information as the already high-dimensional Evo2 22 embeddings. This dimensionality mismatch likely contributed to lower attention being assigned to the structure modality.

representation_rationale.summary: The authors identify dimensionality mismatch as a limitation of the structural representation and a possible cause of its lower attention.

evidence.quote: The  resulting  Genolator  can  interpret  genomic embeddings based on instructions given in English, thereby making the use of embeddings from large genomic models more accessible and paving the way for a new, language-driven interface for interacting with genomic data.

representation_rationale.summary: Natural-language conditioning is intended to make genomic foundation-model embeddings accessible through English instructions.
